title: Residents' Knowledge and Protection Willingness of Otters in a Megacity in China中国特大城市居民对水獭的认知程度及保护意愿
content:
ABSTRACT

In today's rapidly urbanizing world, the survival of wildlife in cities faces significant challenges, and the attitudes of urban residents toward wildlife play a crucial role in their survival. Otters, as top predators in freshwater ecosystems who are highly sensitive to environmental changes, had once gone extinct in Shenzhen—a megacity exemplifying rapid urbanization in China—but reappeared in 2020. We conducted a first field survey on otter population across Shenzhen's river systems, employing transect survey and interviews with local residents to assess both otter population status and residents' knowledge and protection willingness of otters. We did not obtain any reliable records of otter activity during our surveys. Our interviews revealed that 60% of the interviewees knew otters, although only 34% of them correctly identified the image of an otter. Moreover, we found that men and those with more knowledge of general wildlife possessed a higher level of knowledge of otters. Interestingly, we found both low and high levels of otter knowledge associated with stronger protection willingness, whereas intermediate levels of knowledge were linked to weaker support. Our study provides essential baseline data to support future conservation initiatives, such as conservation outreach campaigns and citizen science projects to facilitate the recovery of otter population in Shenzhen.

Abstract

在全球快速城市化的背景下, 城市野生动物的生存面临严峻挑战, 而城市居民对野生动物的态度在其生存中发挥着关键作用。水獭作为淡水生态系统中的顶级捕食者, 对环境变化极为敏感, 曾在中国超大城市深圳灭绝, 但于2020年再次出现。我们在深圳的河流系统开展了首次水獭种群野外调查, 采用样线调查和居民访谈相结合的方法, 评估水獭种群现状以及居民对水獭的了解程度和保护意愿。调查期间未获得可靠的水獭活动记录。访谈结果显示, 60%的受访者听说过水獭, 但仅有34%的受访者能正确辨认水獭图像。此外, 男性和对野生动物了解更多的人群对水獭的了解程度更高。有趣的是, 对水獭了解程度较低和较高的人群均表现出更强的保护意愿, 而了解程度中等的人群保护意愿较弱。本研究为深圳未来的水獭保护工作 (如科普宣传和公民科学项目) 提供了重要的基础数据, 以促进水獭种群的恢复。
